The structure theory of finitely presented A_inf-modules free after inverting p (BMS1 §4.2), with its exact hypotheses: Kedlaya's Lemma 4.6 (vector bundles on the punctured spectrum are free) with Lemmas 4.7–4.8; Lemma 4.9 (for M finitely presented with M[1/p] finite free: M is perfect, M_tor is killed by a power of p and is finitely presented and perfect, M has Tor-dimension at most 2 with Tor_2(M, W(k)) = 0, and Tor_i(M, W(k)) = 0 for i > 0 if M has no x-torsion); Lemma 4.10 with Remark 4.11; Corollary 4.12; and Proposition 4.13 (the functorial sequence 0 → M_tor → M → M_free → M̄ → 0 and the two freeness criteria, the second for K of characteristic 0). AI.2's Lemma 4.26 reduces to the finite free case by Proposition 4.13 and Remark 4.29 rests on Lemma 4.26, while AI.5 requires AI.2. The reviewed nodes CP.5/perfectness-and-tor-bounds-for-ainf-modules and CP.5/ainf-module-structure-theorem become aliases of the AI.2 nodes.

The complex-level specialization lemmas of BMS1 §4.2 for A_inf = W(O_K♭), retaining their hypotheses. Lemma 4.14 concerns finitely presented W_n(O_K♭)-modules. Corollary 4.15 concerns finitely presented A_inf-modules M with M[1/p] free: the two Witt specializations have equal rank and length((M ⊗ W(k))/p^n) ≥ length((M ⊗ W(K♭))/p^n) for every n ≥ 1. Lemma 4.16 concerns C ∈ D(A_inf) with every H^j(C)[1/p] free, without requiring C perfect: H^i(C) ⊗ W(k) → H^i(C ⊗^L W(k)) is injective and becomes bijective after inverting p; absence of x-torsion in H^{i+1}(C) gives an integral bijection. Corollary 4.17 requires C perfect AND every H^j(C)[1/p] free: all cohomology is finitely presented; p-torsion-freeness of H^i(C ⊗^L W(k)) gives finite freeness of H^i(C); integral degreewise base change additionally requires H^{i+1}(C) ⊗ W(k) p-torsion-free. These statements hold for any perfectoid field K. Lemmas 4.18–4.19 and Corollary 4.20 additionally require characteristic 0 and all p-power roots of unity. Lemma 4.18 requires C perfect with all H^j(C)[1/p] free and equates p-torsion-freeness of the two derived specializations in the fixed degree. Lemma 4.19 requires M finitely presented, M[1/(pμ)] finite projective and M ⊗ B_crys^+ finite projective, and concludes M[1/p] finite free. Corollary 4.20 requires C perfect, all H^j(C)[1/(pμ)] free and all H^j(C ⊗^L B_crys^+) free; it gives finite presentation and rational freeness, with the same degree-i freeness and additional degree-(i+1) base-change conditions as Corollary 4.17. Remark 4.21 permits the corresponding de Rham torsion-freeness tests. This review does not certify completion of the partial P7 blueprint.

reviewHistory.notes: The proposal keeps all seven roadmaps and 61 stages, narrows only CP.0 (it imports four coefficient packages) and CP.5 (it imports the generic BMS §4.2 specialization package from AI.5), and names five owners. The report resolves all 95 unordered evidence pairs in one table, as construction-versus-comparison or construction-versus-application relations. Spot checks of the stage texts support this: Q2 imports PR.2 derived prismatic extension, PR.0 compares its envelopes with CR.0 PD envelopes, AI.1 exports Lη to CR.4, and CR.3 keeps only its corrected tower application. Both narrowed layers forward to all consumers. With the twelve accepted restructurings applied, all 16 new links apply and none closes a cycle; the one new reachability, CP.3 -> CP.2, is justified in the report. See REV-RS-01.md.
